title: feat(studio): Fields form designer for the Data pillar — DEFERRED, scope + revisit criteria
body:
## What (deferred)
A WYSIWYG **field-level form designer** inside the Studio Data pillar — the one Data v1 capability deliberately left out of Phase B (objectui#2180). Today the pillar covers: 记录 (runtime grid) / 表单 (section layout designer + preview, #2142) / 验证 (validation rules, #2180) / 设置 (object basics + ADR-0085 semantic roles, #2180). Field CREATION/EDITING flows through the ObjectFieldInspector side panel — functional, but not a drag-first designer for composing a form field-by-field (palette of field types → drop on canvas → configure inline).

## Why deferred (decision record from the builder-ui pillars gap analysis)
- No existing component to compose: the form-layout designer (#2142) reuses `object-fields-io` + fieldGroups semantics, but a palette-driven field composer would be a NEW ~500+ line surface with its own DnD model — not a reuse job.
- The inspector-based flow already covers the 90% (add field → configure type/props in the right panel), and the #2142 layout designer covers arrangement.
- ADR-0085 deliberately keeps grouping/arrangement semantics in `fieldGroups` — a field composer must build on that, not invent a parallel layout model.

## Revisit criteria (any of)
- Dogfood/user feedback that the add-field → inspector round-trip is a measurable friction point for non-technical builders
- The Interfaces pillar grows a page/form composer whose DnD infrastructure can be shared
- AI-authoring flows need a visual confirm surface for generated fields beyond the current layout designer

## Scope sketch when picked up
- Field-type palette (reuse the ObjectFieldInspector type list) + drop-to-create into a fieldGroups section
- Inline rename/required toggles on the canvas; deep config still delegates to ObjectFieldInspector
- Same draft/save/publish flow as the rest of the pillar (one `objDraft`, `client.save(..., {mode:'draft'})`)

Related: builder-ui pillars plan (framework docs), #2142 (layout designer), #2180 (Phase B).
